intro: Today we work on three small things that make your English much clearer: the -s at the end of words (works, plays, watches), short forms like I'm, isn't and don't, and the melody of questions. Listen, copy and say everything out loud!
teachingNotes: Indonesian words don't change, and final consonant clusters are rare, so learners drop the -s (*'She work in a bank'). Stress that the -s is a real sound people listen for: it tells them 'he/she/it' or 'more than one'. Commonest errors: works said as 'work', and watches said as one syllable 'watch-s' instead of WATCH-iz.

Three ways to say -s, decided by the LAST SOUND of the base word, not the spelling: /s/ after p, t, k, f (works, stops, eats); /z/ after vowels and voiced sounds like b, d, g, l, m, n, v (plays, goes, lives, reads); /ɪz/, an extra syllable, after s, z, sh, ch, x and j/ge sounds (watches, washes, fixes, buses, dances, changes). goes and does are spelled -es but have NO extra syllable. Use the throat test (hand on the throat: buzz or no buzz). Accept a slightly weak /z/; the priority is (1) say the -s at all, (2) add the extra syllable where it belongs, and never add one where it doesn't ('work-es', 'like-es').

Contractions: I'm is one syllable (it rhymes with 'time'); isn't = IZ-nt and doesn't = DUZ-nt (the s sounds like z); don't has the o of 'go', not the o of 'on'. The n't carries the 'no', so the n must be heard even when the final t is very light. Short yes answers are never contracted: 'Yes, I am', not 'Yes, I'm'. Only contractions of be and do/does are expected here.

Intonation, as a simple rule for A1: yes/no questions (Are…? Is…? Do…? Does…?) go UP at the end; wh- questions (What, Where, When, Who, How…) go DOWN at the end. Indonesian speakers often rise on every question (Indonesian 'Kamu tinggal di mana?' often rises), so 'Where do you live?' with a rise is the typical error. Don't teach exceptions (friendly rising wh- questions, tag questions).

Use only grammar the learner knows: be, simple present routines, short questions. No past simple (except was/were), no future, no perfect. Phonetic symbols: only /s/, /z/ and /ɪz/; describe everything else in simple words and with the arrows ↗ ↘.

keyPoints.title: Three sounds for -s
keyPoints.explanation: Never drop the -s. Listen to the last sound of the base word: after p, t, k, f the -s is /s/ (works); after a vowel or a 'buzzing' sound it is /z/ (plays, lives); after s, z, sh, ch, x or a j sound it is /ɪz/, an extra syllable (watches = WATCH-iz).

examples.id: Rina main bulu tangkis setiap hari Minggu. (plays: /z/)

examples.en: My father watches the news every evening.
examples.id: Ayahku menonton berita setiap malam. (watches: WATCH-iz)

keyPoints.title: Short forms (contractions)
keyPoints.explanation: In speech we join words: I am → I'm, is not → isn't, do not → don't, does not → doesn't. I'm is one syllable. Say the n of n't clearly: it is the 'no' in the sentence.

examples.en: The office isn't open on Sundays.

keyPoints.title: Questions: up or down?
keyPoints.explanation: Yes/no questions go up at the end ↗ (Are you tired? Do you work here?). Wh- questions go down at the end ↘ (Where do you live? What's your name?).

guidedPractice.prompt: Which verb ends with the sound /s/ (no buzz): eats or lives?
guidedPractice.hint: Put a hand on your throat and say the last sound of 'eat' and 'live'. Which one buzzes?

guidedPractice.prompt: How many syllables does 'buses' have? Write a number.
guidedPractice.hint: bus ends with s, so the -es adds an extra syllable: BUS-iz.

guidedPractice.prompt: Write the short form of 'is not'.
guidedPractice.hint: Join the words and put an apostrophe where the o was. Say it IZ-nt.

guidedPractice.prompt: Write up or down: at the end of 'Do you like coffee?' your voice goes…
guidedPractice.hint: It starts with Do and the answer is yes or no.

independentPractice.prompt: Complete with 'fix' and say the verb with two syllables: My father ___ motorbikes.
independentPractice.hint: fix ends with x (/ks/), so add -es: FIX-iz.

independentPractice.prompt: Say it the natural way. Write it with a short form: He does not work on Sundays.
Write up or down: at the end of 'What time is it?' your voice goes…
independentPractice.hint: It starts with a wh- word: What.

assessment.prompt: Listen. Write the verb you hear.
assessment.listen: Pak Budi teaches English at a school in Bandung.
assessment.rubric: Correct: teaches (TEACH-iz, with an extra syllable). 'teach' = 0 (ending not heard). Spelling slip 'teachs' = 50.

assessment.prompt: Which word has an extra syllable /ɪz/ at the end: goes, closes or plays? Write it.
assessment.rubric: Correct: closes (CLOSE-iz, after a z sound). 'goes' = 0: it is spelled -es but ends with /z/, one syllable. 'plays' = 0.

assessment.prompt: Which verb ends with the sound /s/, with no buzz: reads, likes or calls? Write it.
assessment.rubric: Correct: likes (after k, -s is /s/). 'reads' and 'calls' end with /z/ = 0.

assessment.prompt: Listen. Write the short form (contraction) you hear.
assessment.listen: I don't drink coffee in the evening.
assessment.rubric: Correct: don't. 'do not' = 50 (right meaning, but not the short form you heard). 'doesn't' = 0.

assessment.prompt: Say it the natural way, with a short form. Write: I am not ready.
assessment.rubric: Correct: I'm not ready. 'I amn't ready' = 0 (doesn't exist). 'I am not ready' unchanged = 30.

assessment.prompt: Does your voice go up or down at the end of this question? Write up or down: Where does your brother work?
Does your voice go up or down at the end of this question? Write up or down: Is your office in Jakarta?

blocks.text: In Indonesian, words don't change: *dia bekerja*, *mereka bekerja*. In English, the **-s** is a real sound that people listen for: *she works*, *two books*. So **never drop it**: *She work* sounds wrong. The -s has two quiet sounds. After **p, t, k, f** (no buzz in your throat) it is **/s/**: *works, eats, stops, books*. After a **vowel** or a buzzing sound like **b, d, g, l, m, n, v** it is **/z/**: *plays, goes, lives, reads, bags*.

id.text: Dalam bahasa Indonesia kata tidak berubah: *dia bekerja*, *mereka bekerja*. Dalam bahasa Inggris, **-s** adalah bunyi nyata yang didengarkan orang: *she works*, *two books*. Jadi **jangan pernah menghilangkannya**: *She work* terdengar salah. Akhiran -s punya dua bunyi pendek. Sesudah **p, t, k, f** (leher tidak bergetar) bunyinya **/s/**: *works, eats, stops, books*. Sesudah **vokal** atau bunyi yang bergetar seperti **b, d, g, l, m, n, v** bunyinya **/z/**: *plays, goes, lives, reads, bags*.

blocks.text: The throat test: put a hand on your throat and say *ssss*, then *zzzz*. /z/ buzzes, /s/ doesn't. If /z/ is hard, a soft /s/ is OK at first. The most important thing is to **say the -s**.

id.text: Tes leher: letakkan tangan di leher lalu ucapkan *ssss*, kemudian *zzzz*. /z/ bergetar, /s/ tidak. Kalau /z/ masih sulit, /s/ yang lembut boleh dulu. Yang paling penting adalah **mengucapkan -s-nya**.

blocks.prompt: Which verb ends with the sound /z/ (with a buzz)?
blocks.explain: play ends with a vowel sound, so the -s buzzes: /z/. work and eat end with k and t, so the -s is /s/.

id.explain: play berakhir dengan bunyi vokal, jadi -s-nya bergetar: /z/. work dan eat berakhir dengan k dan t, jadi -s-nya /s/.

blocks.text: After **s, z, sh, ch, x** and a **j** sound (often spelled *ge*), the ending is **/ɪz/** and the word gets **one more syllable**: *watch* → **WATCH-iz**, *wash* → **WASH-iz**, *fix* → **FIX-iz**, *bus* → **BUS-iz**, *change* → **CHANGE-iz**. Saying *watches* as one syllable (*watch-s*) is a very common mistake. Look at the **last sound**, not the spelling: *goes* and *does* end in -es but have **no** extra syllable.

id.text: Sesudah **s, z, sh, ch, x** dan bunyi **j** (sering ditulis *ge*), akhirannya **/ɪz/** dan katanya mendapat **satu suku kata tambahan**: *watch* → **WATCH-iz**, *wash* → **WASH-iz**, *fix* → **FIX-iz**, *bus* → **BUS-iz**, *change* → **CHANGE-iz**. Mengucapkan *watches* sebagai satu suku kata (*watch-s*) adalah kesalahan yang sangat umum. Perhatikan **bunyi terakhir**, bukan ejaannya: *goes* dan *does* berakhiran -es tapi **tidak** punya suku kata tambahan.

blocks.text: Don't add the extra syllable everywhere: *works* and *eats* stay one syllable. Only the 'hissing' sounds s, z, sh, ch, x and j get **-iz**.

id.text: Jangan tambahkan suku kata ekstra di semua kata: *works* dan *eats* tetap satu suku kata. Hanya bunyi 'mendesis' s, z, sh, ch, x dan j yang mendapat **-iz**.

blocks.explain: fix ends with x (/ks/), so -es adds a syllable: FIX-iz, two syllables.

id.explain: fix berakhir dengan x (/ks/), jadi -es menambah satu suku kata: FIX-iz, dua suku kata.

blocks.text: In conversation we join small words: **I am → I'm**, **is not → isn't**, **are not → aren't**, **do not → don't**, **does not → doesn't**. **I'm** is one syllable that rhymes with *time*. **isn't** sounds like **IZ-nt** and **doesn't** like **DUZ-nt**: the s sounds like z. **don't** has the *o* of *go*, not the *o* of *on*. The **n't** means 'not', so say the **n** clearly, or people may hear the opposite.

id.text: Dalam percakapan kita menggabungkan kata-kata kecil: **I am → I'm**, **is not → isn't**, **are not → aren't**, **do not → don't**, **does not → doesn't**. **I'm** satu suku kata yang berima dengan *time*. **isn't** terdengar seperti **IZ-nt** dan **doesn't** seperti **DUZ-nt**: huruf s-nya berbunyi z. **don't** memakai bunyi *o* seperti di *go*, bukan *o* seperti di *on*. **n't** berarti 'tidak', jadi ucapkan **n**-nya dengan jelas, kalau tidak orang bisa mendengar kebalikannya.

blocks.text: Short **yes** answers don't use short forms: *Yes, I am.* / *Yes, she is.*, not *Yes, I'm.* Short **no** answers do: *No, I'm not.* / *No, she isn't.*

id.text: Jawaban singkat **yes** tidak memakai bentuk singkat: *Yes, I am.* / *Yes, she is.*, bukan *Yes, I'm.* Jawaban singkat **no** memakainya: *No, I'm not.* / *No, she isn't.*

blocks.prompt: Why must you say the n in don't and isn't clearly?
options: It makes the sentence a question.
It shows more than one person.
blocks.explain: n't = not. Without it, 'I don't like it' sounds like 'I like it'.

id.explain: n't = not (tidak). Tanpa itu, 'I don't like it' terdengar seperti 'I like it'.

blocks.text: The melody at the end of a question tells people what kind of question it is. **Yes/no questions** start with *Are, Is, Do, Does…* and **go up at the end ↗**: *Are you hungry? Do you work here?* **Wh- questions** start with *What, Where, When, Who, How…* and **go down at the end ↘**: *What's your name? Where do you live?* Many Indonesian speakers go up at the end of every question, because Indonesian questions often rise. In English, a wh- question that goes up can sound surprised or unsure.

id.text: Nada di akhir pertanyaan memberi tahu orang jenis pertanyaannya. **Pertanyaan yes/no** diawali *Are, Is, Do, Does…* dan **naik di akhir ↗**: *Are you hungry? Do you work here?* **Pertanyaan wh-** diawali *What, Where, When, Who, How…* dan **turun di akhir ↘**: *What's your name? Where do you live?* Banyak penutur Indonesia menaikkan nada di akhir setiap pertanyaan, karena pertanyaan bahasa Indonesia sering naik. Dalam bahasa Inggris, pertanyaan wh- yang naik bisa terdengar kaget atau ragu.

blocks.text: A quick test: can you answer with **yes** or **no**? Then go **up** ↗. Do you need information (a name, a place, a time)? Then go **down** ↘.

id.text: Tes cepat: bisakah dijawab dengan **yes** atau **no**? Kalau bisa, nadanya **naik** ↗. Butuh informasi (nama, tempat, waktu)? Kalau begitu, nadanya **turun** ↘.

blocks.prompt: Which question usually goes UP at the end?
blocks.explain: Are you hungry? is a yes/no question, so it goes up. The other two start with wh- words, so they go down.

id.explain: Are you hungry? adalah pertanyaan yes/no, jadi nadanya naik. Dua lainnya diawali kata wh-, jadi nadanya turun.

suggestedQuestions: How do I know if -s sounds like /s/, /z/ or /ɪz/?
Why does 'goes' have no extra syllable?
Is it rude to say 'I am' instead of 'I'm'?
Why does 'Where do you live?' go down at the end?

id.intro: Hari ini kita melatih tiga hal kecil yang membuat bahasa Inggrismu jauh lebih jelas: bunyi -s di akhir kata (works, plays, watches), bentuk singkat seperti I'm, isn't dan don't, serta nada pertanyaan. Dengarkan, tirukan, dan ucapkan semuanya dengan suara keras!
suggestedQuestions: Kenapa 'goes' tidak punya suku kata tambahan?
Apakah tidak sopan mengucapkan 'I am', bukan 'I'm'?
Kenapa nada 'Where do you live?' turun di akhir?

assessment.pe-1: Dengarkan. Tulis kata kerja yang kamu dengar.
assessment.pe-2: Kata mana yang punya suku kata tambahan /ɪz/ di akhir: goes, closes atau plays? Tulis katanya.
assessment.pe-3: Kata kerja mana yang berakhir dengan bunyi /s/, tanpa getaran: reads, likes atau calls? Tulis katanya.
assessment.pe-4: Dengarkan. Tulis bentuk singkat (kontraksi) yang kamu dengar.
assessment.pe-5: Ucapkan dengan cara yang alami, pakai bentuk singkat. Tulis dalam bahasa Inggris: I am not ready.
assessment.pe-6: Apakah suaramu naik atau turun di akhir pertanyaan ini? Tulis up atau down: Where does your brother work?
assessment.pe-7: Apakah suaramu naik atau turun di akhir pertanyaan ini? Tulis up atau down: Is your office in Jakarta?
